BiblicalUsage: This Aramaic word means to go, to depart — and it carries Daniel's story. Daniel went to his house and made the thing known to his companions, he went in to the king and desired time, and the decree went forth to the king's officers. In Ezra it is the same word for the king's command going out and the builders going to Jerusalem.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Daniel's going is my pattern: he went to pray first, and only then went to the king. That order is the whole secret of standing in Babylon.
